distractors.reason: 'Raw' describes food or unprocessed materials, like raw data. We don't say 'raw draft' for an early version of a text.
'Crude' means rude, simple or unrefined, as in crude oil. It is not used to describe an early version of a piece of writing.
'Dirty' describes dirt or rude humour. It has no meaning connected to a draft of an essay.

example_sentence: Before you submit the essay, write a ___ draft and check your paraphrases.
l1_interference: Türkçe konuşanlar 'kaba' yerine 'raw' ya da 'crude' kelimelerini seçebilir, çünkü 'kaba' kelimesinin 'rough' anlamını hemen akla getirmeyebilir. İngilizcede taslak metin için doğru ifade 'rough draft' olur.
explanation: In English, 'rough' describes a first version that is not finished or polished. It is used with drafts, sketches, and estimates, and it signals that the text will still be revised.

related_collocations.example: The key idea of the article is simple.
Give a brief summary of the text.
An accurate paraphrase keeps the original meaning.

memory_tip: ROUGH DRAFT = an early version that is not finished | RAW = unprocessed (raw data, raw vegetables)
